turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Thanks. Well, I came in today because... the thought of getting on an airplane just scares me so bad right now. I mean, I know in my head it doesn't make any sense, I really do, but... my whole body just tells me that the plane is going to fall. It's just really bad, and I don't know what to do about it.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes an intense, irrational fear of getting on an airplane, acknowledging that the fear does not make sense but feeling physically terrified that the plane will fall.

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience this kind of intense fear or panic in any other situations, or is it only related to flying?
turns.patient_response: No, it's really just flying. I mean, I can ride in elevators, I can drive on the highway, I don't have any problems with heights or anything like that. It's... it's strictly airplanes. When I'm not thinking about flying, I'm completely fine.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms that their intense fear is strictly limited to a specific situation, which is flying in airplanes.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been dealing with this intense fear of flying?
turns.patient_response: It's been going on for about seven months now. Um, it started right after I lost my clinic job. I had to take a flight on this small plane, and it was just... incredibly turbulent. Really rough. And ever since that specific flight, I've just been terrified of getting back on one.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient explicitly states being 'terrified of getting back on' a plane, indicating a marked fear of a specific situation (flying).
